basis: Absent functional peripheral T lymphocytes define this immune and blood-cell disorder; secondary respiratory and enteric infections do not establish additional organ involvement.

decisions.haematologic: primary: deficiency of functional T lymphocytes is a defining blood-cell abnormality.

basis: Ptosis, neurodevelopmental impairment and metopic/craniosynostosis abnormalities define the syndrome; hearing impairment and cardiac defects are occasional.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental impairment is a core syndrome feature, supported by frequent developmental, speech and motor delays.

basis: Severe inherited demyelinating neuropathy; persistent foot deformities and denervation atrophy affect most patients. Ocular findings are occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed foot deformities and muscle wasting affect most patients; this exceeds weakness alone and does not depend on the single-patient scoliosis annotation.

basis: Macroglossia, abdominal wall defects, lateralized overgrowth and persistent hyperinsulinism are major diagnostic features; transient hypoglycemia and tumor risk add no organs.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: persistent hyperinsulinism is a cardinal diagnostic feature; this does not rely on transient neonatal hypoglycemia.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized skeletal overgrowth and abdominal wall defects are major defining structural abnormalities.

basis: Encephalopathy, amyotrophy and optic atrophy define the syndrome; amyotrophy occurs in 6/6, optic atrophy in 2/6 and scoliosis in 3/6.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: amyotrophy is explicitly syndrome-defining and present in 6/6; scoliosis in 3/6 provides additional structural evidence.

basis: Hypereosinophilic collagen disorder; cardiac disease is not established as defining or present in at least 30%. Broad cardiomyopathy ancestry alone is insufficient.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: restrictive cardiomyopathy is inherited through the broad hypereosinophilic-syndrome ancestry; no concept-specific defining cardiac feature or frequency of at least 30% is supplied.

basis: The supplied definition explicitly describes excessive thrombi, establishing vascular thrombosis as well as a coagulation disorder; downstream organ infarctions are not assumed.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the supplied definition specifies excessive thrombi, making vascular thrombosis defining rather than merely a later risk.

basis: Lung, diaphragm and distal limb defects define it; renal dysplasia and severe developmental impairment each 80-99%. Cardiac, ocular, oral and nail anomalies omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: severe developmental impairment occurs in 80-99%, with frequent brain malformations; the defining core comprises diaphragm, lung and distal limb abnormalities.

basis: Lipodystrophy, diabetes, skin papules, cardiomyopathy and liver steatosis define it. Hepatic involvement occupies the fourth axis under the primary cap; frequencies unspecified.

decisions.hepatic: involved: steatosis is a defining manifestation, retained as the fourth axis because primary is capped at three; no frequency estimate is supplied.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is explicitly syndrome-defining and warrants priority among the three primary axes.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with leukodystrophy; contractures and visual impairment each occur in 30-79%. Optic atrophy is occasional; respiratory failure alone does not establish lung damage.

decisions.ocular: involved: visual impairment represents loss of function and is frequent (30-79%); occasional optic atrophy does not negate the broader visual impairment annotation.
